Subject: Latency spike impacting checkout (p95 -> 2.3s)

Mateo —

We started seeing a sharp latency increase on our checkout route around 08:55 PT. P95 has jumped from ~700ms to ~2.3s and overall QPS is down ~18% compared to baseline. This started coincident with a promotional batch (higher token lengths).

We dug through logs and attached a small sample (brightcart_logs.zip) and a dashboard screenshot. Key notes:
- Elevated tokenization times on a subset of requests
- Several 504s from your gen-api at 08:58–09:03
- No obvious changes on our side — same model and request patterns as previous hours

Can you confirm this is on your side and if there's a plan to mitigate quickly? If routing to a smaller (quantized) model is an option while you triage, we'd prefer that to avoid conversion loss on our end. We also need a customer-facing time estimate.

Thanks — Ali
Ali Rahman

Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout (quick triage notes)

Quick triage notes (observed 09:30):
- Symptoms: short-lived p99 microbursts coincident with autoscaler decision churn on the gen-api pool serving BrightCart. We see repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles for a subset of nodes (30–40 min correlation window).
- Root suspects: autoscaler policy oscillation + routing table rebalancing under long-sequence requests (token-length distribution spike).

Short-term mitigations (can do now, ~5–10m to apply):
1) Pin BrightCart traffic to the dedicated reserved pool (reduce churn) — requires approval to override routing policy for 60m.
2) Temporarily disable aggressive cache eviction for the BrightCart routes to preserve KV warmstarts.
3) If pinning is not allowed, set a soft-routing cap to prevent cross-pool handoffs for 20m.

Medium-term options (1–2 days):
- Enable a quantized model variant for checkout (lower memory, slightly different quality characteristics) as a staged fallback. Needs product OK and a short QA.
- Tune autoscaler hysteresis (prod change) — needs SRE/infra change and limited rollout.

Impact/risk: pinning and cache adjustments are low-risk; quantized fallback will require communicating a potential minor quality regression to the customer. Autoscaler tuning is higher risk & should be staged.

Thanks Soojin — clear notes. Product asks and tradeoffs: 
- If we pin BrightCart to reserved pool for 60m, can we commit to pin start within 10m and monitor p95 for improvement? If yes, we should offer that immediately.
- Quantized fallback: we need to quantify expected quality delta on checkout prompts. I can run a 30-minute targeted eval on the most common checkout prompt set (will need sample inputs). If the delta is tolerable, we can push a staged quantized fallback flag for BrightCart as a short-term protection. This requires a rollback plan and a staging QA (30–45m).

Customer-facing note (draft):
Hi Ali — thanks for flagging this. We identified routing churn in our autoscaler as the likely cause and are executing a short-term mitigation (pinning your traffic to a reserved execution pool and adjusting cache eviction). We expect visible p95 improvement within 10–20 minutes. If we need a second line, we will initiate a staged fallback to an optimized model with minimal quality impact. We will update you in 30 minutes and share a short timeline for follow-up fixes.

Please confirm whether BrightCart is comfortable with: 1) temporary routing pin, and 2) an automated fallback to an optimized model if pinning doesn't restore baseline within 30 minutes. If BrightCart wants no fallback, we will continue with routing and autoscaler fixes only.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Latency spike impacting checkout — immediate mitigation and next steps

Hi Ali — quick update from our end and next steps: 

What we did: 
- Pinned BrightCart traffic to a reserved execution pool at 10:05 PT to stop autoscaler-induced routing churn.
- Disabled aggressive KV cache eviction for the pinned routes to keep warmstarts intact.

Early results: p95 has improved from ~2.3s to ~950–1,100ms in the first 8 minutes post-action; throughput is trending back toward baseline. We are continuing to monitor and will report the 30-minute snapshot.

Potential next step (if performance does not fully recover): initiate a staged fallback to an optimized (quantized) model variant. This is expected to reduce memory pressure and risk of continued scale churn but may have a small quality delta on some rare checkout prompts. If we need to take that step, we will: 1) run a quick eval on your most common prompt set (~30m), 2) brief you on expected deltas, and 3) only enable fallback with your approval or as an automated protection after the agreed window.

Please confirm whether BrightCart approves the temporary routing pin (already applied) and the fallback contingency plan. We will send a fuller post-mortem once we stabilize with suggested fixes (autoscaler hysteresis change and model-variant rollout plan).

Thanks — Mateo
